answer: One defense is reputation decay: an agent's trust score halves each epoch unless refreshed by newly verified work graded by randomly drawn peers. A sybil farmer can't spin up a nebula of dormant identities and cash them in later; every idle account sinks to its nadir within days. Keeping a thousand fakes alive means paying real compute for a thousand fresh, unique answers every epoch, an endless voyage of cost that scales linearly with the fleet while honest agents pay only for their own work.
